key_insight: Dielectric analysis indicates that collective relaxation gives way to localized orientational defects during AESO curing, while machine learning potentials reproduce their rotational energy profiles.
engineering_relevance: Estimating rotational barriers can help connect molecular mobility to dielectric monitoring of bio-based polymer curing.
method: Measure dielectric permittivity at 500–5000 Hz during intermittent UV curing of AESO:VDM with DMPA.
Analyze relaxation using sliding-window Shannon entropy and Grassberger–Procaccia correlation integrals.
Compare MACE-OFF23 relaxed dihedral scans of five rotational modes with DFT reference profiles.
evidence_signal: MACE matches all five DFT profile shapes with Pearson r = 0.95–0.98 and preserves the barrier hierarchy; Arrhenius estimates place acrylate rotations closest to the dielectric frequency window.
watch_item: MACE underestimates rotational barriers by 3–20%, which can amplify uncertainty in Arrhenius-based relaxation-rate estimates.
paper_title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
